rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout cannot faithfully determine partial progress. The continuity check only distinguishes the original mug being to the right from certain cases where it was not moved toward the target; it leaves other non-complete placements unresolved, and no support check separately establishes whether the original mug moved closer to the right without reaching it. Thus the program can report unknown where the rubric requires partial for evidenced progress, or cannot distinguish no progress from progress in relevant cases. The broad visibility check and current-position check do not supply that missing evidence.

The fulfillment readout cannot reliably compose the evidence: `s2` is a support check whose criteria already assign complete/absent/partial/unknown, while `original_mug_progress` separately assesses source-anchored movement. The readout does not specify how to resolve conflicting observations from these checks. In particular, `s2` can pass because a mug is right of the headphones even when the source-anchored check fails, and its own criteria call that complete despite the readout correctly requiring the original mug. This overlapping completion rule risks unsupported completion. The source-anchored check otherwise appropriately distinguishes progress from a right-side mug alone.

The fulfillment rule is too restrictive for the original rubric: it requires source_mug_continuity to pass before completion, although the instruction asks only that the mug be to the right of the headphones. A visible mug in the requested position can establish fulfillment without proving source-object continuity. It also makes partial progress depend on evidence about the source mug, so genuine movement toward the requested position can remain unknown when continuity is unresolved. The support checks otherwise assess the requested relation without imposing an editing technique.
